# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 106 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 106 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_106_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — Final Identifications

**1** I saw the tower and the lord of the tower, and everyone who was building it was glorifying the Lord with great enthusiasm. **2** I asked the Shepherd standing beside me, "Who is the lord of the tower?" "The Son of God," he said. **3** "And the six men with the virgins?" "Those are the holy angels of the Lord. The virgins are the holy spirits." **4** "And the young men building the tower?" "Also holy angels of the Lord — but the six are over them. Everyone who builds the tower will enter God's kingdom. **5** Even those who just brought the stones will enter the kingdom, provided they live in the truth." **6** "What about those who brought stones but couldn't fit them in?" **7** "These believed but walked away because they were wavering," he said. "They weren't built into the tower because they were torn between commitment and doubt, and malice had taken hold of them. **8** They will not enter God's kingdom." **9** "And the round stones that don't fit anywhere?" **10** "These too are believers," he said, "but they have great worldly wealth. When hardship comes, their money and business dealings cause them to turn away from the Lord." **11** "When will they ever qualify for the tower?" I asked. **12** "When the riches that have trapped their souls are stripped away — then they'll become useful to the Lord. **13** Just as a round stone can only be made square by cutting something away, the wealthy can only become useful to God by losing their wealth. **14** Learn from your own experience: when you were wealthy you were of no use. Now you are genuinely useful — you count for life."

---

*PNEUMA renders the repeated round-stone maxim as lived wisdom, connecting it directly to Hermas's biographical testimony.*
